references.text: In Leviticus, detailed instructions are given about the Sabbath year, where the land must rest every seventh year after six years of sowing and harvesting, expanding on the principle from Exodus 23:10.
The Lord promises blessing in the sixth year to compensate for the rest during the Sabbath year, demonstrating God's care for the people's needs while obeying the command to sow for six years.
Moses repeats the principle of a seven-year cycle, here linked to the remission of debts, which corresponds with the agricultural seven-year cycle in Exodus 23:10.
Instructions about harvesting and leaving something for the poor, expanding on the social dimension of the agricultural laws mentioned in Exodus 23:10.
A reference to the seven-year cycle in connection with the public reading of the law, confirming the ongoing validity of the Sabbath year arrangement.
This reference expands on the six-year period by including vineyard work and introduces the law concerning the Sabbath year.
Leviticus 25:21 provides the theological basis (God's blessing) for being able to follow the commandment of six years of sowing before the Sabbath year.
